source.title: Advancing Bug Detection in Fastjson2 with Large Language Models Driven Unit Test Generation
source.authors: Zhiyuan Zhong; Si-Nan Wang; Hailong Wang; Shaojin Wen; Hao Guan; Yida Tao; Ye-Pang Liu

record.file_problem: Full text is present, with minor PDF-extraction formatting artifacts. The supplied title differs from the title in the paper text; the arXiv identifier matches.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares LLMs on unit-test generation outcomes, a downstream code-generation task, but does not measure pretraining loss or conduct a controlled scale sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test language-model loss scaling, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, architecture effects, other modalities, or fit dependence. Its comparison of test-generation coverage across LLMs bears only on V6. The paper's other coverage comparisons, bug counts, and test-validator results concern the proposed software-testing method, not scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: The paper builds a multi-agent unit-test generator (JSONATG) for fastjson and reports its own method's coverage and bug counts. Table IV compares three Test Programmer LLMs as an ablation of the pipeline. These are different families with different training data, size is unstated for GPT-3.5, and there is no scale sweep and no loss. So it does not test whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale or loss (V6), or any other version. It uses LLMs as tools and reports only its own method's performance, which makes it T4, not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it should lead with the main conclusion: JSONATG beats ChatTester and ChatUniTest in coverage on complex fastjson classes and found 59 bugs (47 confirmed, 28 fixed). In the model ablation, GPT-3.5 gave the highest coverage, and DeepSeek-6.7B performed comparably. Llama3 was lowest, attributed to its higher compile-error rate (25.71%). Different models found distinct bugs.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates LLM-generated unit-test coverage across three models; it does not fit or evaluate language-model pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Coverage varies by Test Programmer model and fastjson class; the paper also reports different compile-error rates across models.
record.problems: Only three Test Programmer models are compared; GPT-3.5 size is not stated, and the models are not a controlled scale series. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the coverage values. The measured outcome is software-library test coverage, not held-out language-model loss.

untested.parts: All: no scale series or loss relation; only three heterogeneous models are compared as a pipeline ablation.

record.verdict_notes: A software-engineering paper unrelated to scaling laws. The reader's V6 'tests' link and limits_scope label are removed. The remark that a smaller model rivals GPT-3.5 is anecdotal, since GPT-3.5's size is unstated.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run losses from smaller-run fits.
Architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior across other modalities or training regimes.
The study reports unit-test-generation coverage for three LLMs, but does not relate performance to pretraining loss or establish a controlled relationship with model scale.
Sensitivity of scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation to setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: Llama3
rows.operation_detail: Used as the Test Programmer LLM to generate unit tests; instruction-tuned and configured with top-p 0.95 and temperature 0.8.
rows.note: Three tests were generated per original bug-triggering test. Coverage is a downstream test-generation outcome, not a direct language-model loss or controlled scale measure.
rows.check: Ablation of the study's own pipeline (Test Programmer LLM choice, Table IV), not a scale series. Llama3-8B, DeepSeek-6.7B and GPT-3.5 (size unknown) differ in family and training, so coverage cannot bear on scale or loss predictability. The same applies to r2–r18.
